title: Drones hit Yandex data centre in first major attack on Russian data hub
source_used: NBC News (carries the Reuters report, 'By Reuters')
key_facts: Drones hit a major data center in Russia's Ryazan region owned by Yandex, the company said on Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
Yandex is described in the report as Russia's leading artificial intelligence and technology company.
The attack caused a fire and forced Yandex to fully suspend operations at the center.
Yandex said its core consumer services were not affected; it runs YandexGPT, one of Russia's leading generative AI models.
On its Yandex Cloud website the company reported electricity supply problems in one data center zone and advised customers to use other zones.
The attack followed a wave of Russian attacks on Ukrainian data centres in recent weeks.
The report says there were previously no confirmed major Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian data centers.
The report does not say who launched the drones.
quote_evidence: The company said that its core consumer services were not affected.
Previously there were no confirmed major Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian data centers.
why_it_matters_hint: A drone strike took a major AI company's data centre offline, showing that AI data centres can be physically hit in the war.
